rationale: Both correctly identify the core issue (the ground-truth's central point: fork_rng lacks device_type and device_module isn't derived from parameter.device, which the human reviewer's own comment confirms was intentionally CUDA/MUSA-only, not a broad allowlist). X presents this with clean, verified reasoning, concrete diffs, and reasonable actionable fixes; it also independently catches the FL2VA/Ref2VA copy-paste doc bug that Y also found. Y covers similar ground but buries findings in dense, hard-to-parse evidence dumps with excessive citation noise, an unresolved 'FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED' non-verdict, and some low-value nit findings (unverifiable AMD CI claims, speculative torch version floor) that hurt precision and actionability. Neither candidate hits the exact ground-truth nuance (that CUDA-only behavior was deliberately preserved and only MUSA was added after hardware validation), but X's suggested fix (allowlist cuda/musa) aligns closer to the maintainer's actual intent than Y's more diffuse treatment.
